summary: Z9 EarthScope is a climate research and data visualization project that explores long-term temperature and precipitation trends using NASA POWER data. The project analyzes historical monthly climate observations for locations in Pakistan, including Islamabad, Lahore, Karachi, and Mithi. It applies statistical methods to identify possible climate trends and presents the findings through a web-based research platform. By making climate data easier to explore and understand, Z9 EarthScope aims to support climate awareness and data-driven understanding of regional environmental changes.
details:
Overview

Z9 EarthScope is a web-based climate research platform designed to explore historical climate patterns and identify long-term temperature and precipitation trends across selected locations in Pakistan.

How It Works

The platform retrieves historical monthly meteorological data from NASA's Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources (POWER) project. It analyzes climate variables for Islamabad, Lahore, Karachi, and Mithi across different historical periods.

The research archive includes:

  • Historical monthly climate observations
  • Annual summaries and trend visualizations
  • Seasonal Mann–Kendall trend analysis
  • Seasonal Sen's slope estimation
  • Statistical significance information
  • Reproducible research records and data provenance

Technology and Methodology

The project uses web development technologies including Next.js, TypeScript, and modern web technologies. NASA POWER data is processed using JavaScript-based analysis scripts. Statistical methods are used to estimate the direction, magnitude, and significance of observed trends.

Purpose and Potential Impact

Z9 EarthScope makes climate information more accessible through an interactive research interface. It can help students, researchers, and interested users explore historical climate patterns and understand why long-term climate monitoring matters.

Creativity and Development

The project combines NASA climate data, statistical analysis, and web-based visualization into one research platform. I independently carried out most of the project work, including the concept, research, implementation, and presentation, with AI assistance.

The platform presents data-derived findings rather than claiming to provide weather forecasts or definitive climate attribution. Its results should be interpreted with the documented data and methodological limitations.
